skill.name: image-compress
skill.description: Compress local images through a remote MCP service and receive file-size comparisons, compression ratios, and CDN URLs.
skill.summary: Batch-compress local images with configurable quality through a remote MCP endpoint.
skill.author: xiaowu89

security_audit.summary: Most command and obfuscation alerts are Markdown or JavaScript syntax false positives. Confirmed risks include remote image transmission, plaintext credential handling, and unsafe value interpolation. Security changes are required before publication.

remediation.issue: Configuration commands print complete project or home MCP files, which can expose unrelated credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Parse the JSON locally and retrieve only the named server fields without printing secrets to tool output.

remediation.issue: Paths, URLs, and API keys are inserted directly into executable JavaScript string literals.
remediation.suggestion: Pass values through environment variables or structured input, then validate types, paths, and HTTPS URLs.

remediation.issue: The download command interpolates output paths and service-provided URLs into a shell command.
remediation.suggestion: Use a structured HTTP client or spawn curl with an argument array after validating the destination and URL.

remediation.issue: Images and an API key are sent to a remote endpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit upload consent, document data retention, and restrict requests to approved HTTPS endpoints.

remediation.issue: API key acquisition is directed to a personal WeChat account.
remediation.suggestion: Provide an official service page with published ownership, privacy, support, and credential-issuance policies.

content.user_title: Compress Images with a Remote Service
content.value_statement: Large images consume storage and slow content delivery. This skill sends selected images to an MCP compression service and reports optimized CDN results.
actual_capabilities: Processes one local image or supported images in a selected folder.
Supports PNG, JPG, JPEG, WebP, BMP, and TGA input extensions.
Skips files larger than the service limit of 5 MB.
Sends compression requests with a configurable quality from 1 to 100.
Runs up to five compression requests concurrently.
Reports original size, compressed size, ratio, status, and CDN URL.
limitations: Requires Node.js 18 or later, an MCP endpoint, and a valid NX_API_KEY.
Uploads local image contents to a remote service.
Does not compress files larger than 5 MB.
Does not replace original files unless the user separately downloads results.

use_cases.title: Optimize Website Assets
use_cases.description: Compress a folder of website images and collect CDN URLs before deployment.

use_cases.title: Reduce Editorial Uploads
use_cases.description: Reduce image sizes before publishing articles while retaining a clear result summary.

use_cases.title: Prepare Design Exports
use_cases.description: Compare compression ratios across exported PNG, JPEG, and WebP assets.

prompt_templates.title: Compress One Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Compress {image_path} with the configured service. Report the original size, compressed size, ratio, and CDN URL.

prompt_templates.title: Compress a Folder
prompt_templates.prompt: Compress supported images in {folder_path} at quality {quality}. Skip unsupported files and summarize every result.

prompt_templates.title: Compress and Download
prompt_templates.prompt: Compress {image_path} at quality {quality}. After showing the result, download the compressed file to {output_path}.

prompt_templates.title: Process a Production Batch
prompt_templates.prompt: Review {folder_path}, list eligible files, confirm remote upload, then compress at quality {quality}. Report failures, total savings, and CDN URLs.

output_examples.output: product-photo.jpg: 1.8 MB original, 620 KB compressed, 65.6% reduction. The remote service returned a CDN URL.

output_examples.input: Compress all supported images in the campaign folder.
output: 1 image exceeded the 5 MB service limit.

output_examples.input: Compress icon.png and download the result.
output_examples.output: icon.png compressed successfully. The result was downloaded to the requested destination after the CDN URL was returned.

best_practices: Review the selected files and confirm remote upload before compression.
Use project-scoped configuration and protect credential files with restrictive permissions.
Start with quality 90, then compare visual quality and file-size savings.
anti_patterns: Do not process confidential images without approval for third-party upload.
Do not print complete MCP configuration files or API keys.
Do not insert untrusted paths, URLs, or credentials directly into shell commands.

faq.question: Which image formats are supported?
faq.answer: The workflow accepts PNG, JPG, JPEG, WebP, BMP, and TGA file extensions.

faq.question: Does the skill compress images locally?
faq.answer: No. It reads local files and sends their contents to a remote MCP compression service.

faq.question: What configuration is required?
faq.answer: You need Node.js 18 or later, an MCP service URL, and a valid NX_API_KEY.

faq.question: What is the maximum file size?
faq.answer: The documented service limit is 5 MB per image. Larger files are skipped.

faq.question: Are original files changed?
faq.answer: No. Compression returns CDN URLs, and local download is a separate optional step.

faq.question: Can I change compression quality?
faq.answer: Yes. The quality parameter accepts values from 1 to 100 and defaults to 90.
